preface.p: Australian National Registry of Emissions Units Act 2011
This is a compilation of the Australian National Registry of Emissions Units Act 2011 that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 14 October 2024 (the compilation date).
The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au). The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. For more information on any uncommenced amendments, see the Register for the compiled law.

p.b: Application, saving and transitional provisions for provisions and amendments

section.heading: Electronic notice transmitted to the Regulator

content.p: (1) For the purposes of this Act, a notice is an electronic notice transmitted to the Regulator if, and only if:
the notice is transmitted to the Regulator by means of an electronic communication; and

if the Regulator requires that the notice be transmitted, in accordance with particular information technology requirements, by means of a particular kind of electronic communication—the Regulator’s requirement has been met; and
the notice complies with regulations made for the purposes of subsection (2).
The regulations may make provision for or in relation to the security and authenticity of notices transmitted to the Regulator by means of an electronic communication.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (2) may deal with:
encryption; and
authentication of identity.
Subsection (3) does not limit subsection (2).

For the purposes of this Act, if a notice is transmitted to the Regulator by means of an electronic communication, the notice is taken to have been transmitted on the day on which the electronic communication is dispatched.
(6) Subsection (5) of this section has effect despite section 14A of the Electronic Transactions Act 1999.
(7) This section does not, by implication, limit the regulations that may be made under the Electronic Transactions Act 1999.
This Act binds the Crown in each of its capacities.
This Act does not make the Crown liable to a pecuniary penalty or to be prosecuted for an offence.

part.heading: Australian National Registry of Emissions Units

content.p: The following is a simplified outline of this Part:
• The Australian National Registry of Emissions Units is continued in existence.
• The Regulator may, in accordance with the regulations, open a Registry account in the name of a person.
• A person may, in accordance with the regulations, request the Regulator to close the person’s Registry account.
• The Regulator is empowered to make corrections to the Registry.
• A person may apply to the Federal Court for the rectification of the Registry.

division.heading: Australian National Registry of Emissions Units

section.heading: Australian National Registry of Emissions Units

content.p: The register:
known as the Australian National Registry of Emissions Units; and
that was in existence under the executive power of the Commonwealth immediately before the commencement of this section;
continues in existence as a register under this Act under the name Australian National Registry of Emissions Units.
The Registry is to be kept by the Regulator.
Note: In this Act, Registry means the Australian National Registry of Emissions Units—see section 4.
The Registry is to be maintained by electronic means.
The purposes of the Registry are as follows:
to be a registry for:
Australian carbon credit units; and
safeguard mechanism credit units;
to be Australia’s national registry for Kyoto units.
The regulations may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to open accounts within the Registry.
An account opened under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) is to be opened in the name of a particular person.
(3) An account kept in the name of a person is to be known as a Registry account of the person.
(4) Each Registry account is to be identified by a unique number, to be known as the account number of the Registry account.
A person may have 2 or more Registry accounts.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for or in relation to any or all of the following matters:
requests to open Registry accounts;
the approval by the Regulator of a form for such a request;
information that must accompany such a request;
the fee (if any) that must accompany such a request;
verification by statutory declaration of statements in such a request;
empowering the Regulator:
to require a person who makes such a request to give the Regulator further information in connection with such a request; and
if the person breaches the requirement—to refuse to consider the request, or to refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the request.
Subsection (6) does not limit subsection (1).
A fee mentioned in paragraph (6)(d) must not be such as to amount to taxation.
Note 1: See also section 11 (identification procedures).
Note 2: See also section 16 (unilateral closure of Registry accounts).
The regulations may prescribe identification procedures that must be carried out by the Regulator before the Regulator opens a Registry account in the name of the person.
(2) The regulations may declare that a specified number is a transaction limit for the purposes of this section.
The regulations may make provision for identifying Registry accounts that are subject to a transaction limit.
An identification procedure prescribed under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1):
may be expressed to apply to Registry accounts that are subject to a transaction limit; or
may be expressed to apply to Registry accounts that are not subject to a transaction limit.
The regulations may provide that, if a Registry account is subject to a particular transaction limit, the Regulator must not:
issue to the account any:
Australian carbon credit units; or
safeguard mechanism credit units; or
comply with an instruction to transfer units to the account;
if doing so would result in the account having entries for a number of units that exceeds the transaction limit.
The regulations may empower the Regulator to designate a Commonwealth Registry account as an account with a name specified in the regulations.

section.heading: Opening of new Commonwealth Registry accounts

content.p: The regulations may empower the Minister to direct the Regulator to:
open a Registry account in the name of the Commonwealth; and
give that Registry account the designation specified in the direction.

section.heading: Units in certain accounts cannot be transferred

content.p: The regulations may provide that, if there is an entry for a Kyoto unit in a specified Commonwealth Registry account, the unit cannot be transferred.
(2) Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) have effect despite any other provision of this Act or the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011.
The regulations may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to close a Registry account kept in the name of a person.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to close a Registry account unless:
the person, by written notice given to the Regulator, requests the Regulator to close the account; and
there are no entries for any Australian carbon credit units in the account; and
there are no entries for any Kyoto units in the account; and
there are no entries for any safeguard mechanism credit units in the account.

section.heading: Unilateral closure of Registry accounts etc.

content.p: The regulations may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to close a Registry account kept in the name of a person.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to close a Registry account unless:
the person has contravened, or is contravening, this Part or regulations made for the purposes of this Part; and
at least 30 days before closing the account, the Regulator gives the person a written notice:
stating that the Regulator proposes to close the account; and
setting out the effect of any regulations made for the purposes of subsections (3), (4) and (6); and
setting out the effect of any legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (5).
Cancellation or transfer of units

The regulations may provide that, if immediately before the Regulator closes a Registry account under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1), there is an entry for an Australian carbon credit unit in the account, the unit is cancelled.

The regulations may provide that, if immediately before the Regulator closes a Registry account under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1), there is an entry for a Kyoto unit in the account, the Regulator must transfer the unit to a voluntary cancellation account.

The legislative rules may provide that if, immediately before the Regulator closes a Registry account under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1), there is an entry for a safeguard mechanism credit unit in the account, then the Regulator must take such action in relation to the unit as is specified in the legislative rules.
Refusal of request to open new Registry account
The regulations may provide that, if:
the Regulator has closed a person’s Registry account under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) of this section; and
the person requests the Regulator, under regulations made for the purposes of subsection 10(1), to open a Registry account in the name of the person;
the Regulator must, under regulations made for the purposes of subsection 10(1), refuse the request.
Record
The Registry must set out a record of:
each closure under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1); and
each cancellation under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (3); and
each action taken under legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (5).
Australian carbon credit units
(1) An entry for an Australian carbon credit unit in a Registry account may be made in accordance with the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011.
Kyoto units
An entry for a Kyoto unit in a Registry account may be made in accordance with this Act.
Safeguard mechanism credit units
An entry for a safeguard mechanism credit unit in a Registry account may be made in accordance with this Act.

division.heading: Change in name of account holder

section.heading: Change in name of account holder

content.p: The regulations may provide that, if:
a Registry account is kept in the name of a person; and
the name of the person has changed; and
the person applies in writing to the Regulator to have the new name substituted for the previous name in the Registry in relation to the account;
the Regulator may make the necessary alterations in the Registry.

section.heading: Corrections of clerical errors, obvious defects or unauthorised entries etc.

content.p: Power of correction
The Regulator may alter the Registry for the purposes of correcting:
a clerical error or an obvious defect in the Registry; or
an entry made in the Registry without sufficient cause; or
an entry wrongly existing in the Registry; or
an entry wrongly removed from the Registry.
The Regulator may exercise the power conferred by subsection (1):
on written application being made to the Regulator by a person; or
on the Regulator’s own initiative.
The Regulator must not exercise the power conferred by subsection (1) of this section in a manner contrary to a decision of the Federal Court in proceedings under section 22.
The Regulator must not exercise the power conferred by subsection (1) of this section in a manner contrary to:
regulations made for the purposes of section 32A of this Act; or
section 48A of this Act; or
(b) section 150A of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011.
Publication of alteration
If the Regulator makes an alteration to the Registry under subsection (1), the Regulator must cause to be published on the Regulator’s website a notice setting out the details of the alteration.
Refusal
If:
the Regulator decides to refuse to alter the Registry under subsection (1); and
the Regulator made the decision in response to an application;
the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant.

section.heading: General power of correction of Registry—Kyoto units

content.p: Power of correction
The Regulator may make such alterations to the Registry as the Regulator considers appropriate for the purposes of ensuring that the relevant provisions of the Kyoto rules are complied with.
The Regulator may exercise the power conferred by subsection (1):
on written application being made to the Regulator by a person; or
on the Regulator’s own initiative.
Publication of alteration
If the Regulator makes an alteration to the Registry under subsection (1), the Regulator must cause to be published on the Regulator’s website a notice setting out the details of the alteration.
Refusal
If:
the Regulator decides to refuse to alter the Registry under subsection (1); and
the Regulator made the decision in response to an application;
the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant.
Application for rectification by aggrieved person
If a person is aggrieved by any of the following:
the omission of an entry from the Registry;
an entry made in the Registry without sufficient cause;
an entry wrongly existing in the Registry;
an error or defect in an entry in the Registry;
an entry wrongly removed from the Registry;
the person may apply to the Federal Court for the rectification of the Registry.
Application for rectification by the Regulator
If the Regulator is concerned about any of the following:
the omission of an entry from the Registry;
an entry made in the Registry without sufficient cause;
an entry wrongly existing in the Registry;
an error or defect in an entry in the Registry;
an entry wrongly removed from the Registry;
the Regulator may apply to the Federal Court for the rectification of the Registry.
Court orders

If an application is made under subsection (1) or (2) to the Federal Court for the rectification of the Registry, the court may make such order as it thinks fit directing the rectification of the Registry.
An order made by the court must not be expressed to take effect before the order is made.
The court must not make an order that is contrary to:
regulations made for the purposes of section 32A of this Act; or
section 48A of this Act; or
(b) section 150A of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011.
In proceedings under this section, the court may decide any question that it is necessary or expedient to decide in connection with the rectification of the Registry.
Appearance of Regulator
Notice of an application under subsection (1) must be given to the Regulator, whose representative:
may appear and be heard; and
must appear if so directed by the court.
Copy of order to be given to Regulator
An office copy of an order made by the court may be given to the Regulator.
Compliance with order
The Regulator must, on receipt of the order, rectify the Registry accordingly.

section.heading: Making a false entry in the Registry

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person:
makes an entry in the Registry; or
causes an entry to be made in the Registry; or
concurs in the making of an entry in the Registry; and
the person does so knowing that the entry is false.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 7 years or 2,000 penalty units, or both.
Note: The same conduct may be an offence against both this section and section 145.4 of the Criminal Code.
A person commits an offence if:
the person produces or tenders in evidence a document; and
the document falsely purports to be a copy of or extract from an entry in the Registry.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months or 60 penalty units, or both.
Note: The same conduct may be an offence against both this section and section 137.2 of the Criminal Code.
The Regulator may supply a copy of or extract from the Registry certified by the Regulator to be a true copy or true extract, as the case may be.
Note: See also section 155 of the Evidence Act 1995.
The Regulator may charge a fee specified in the regulations for supplying a certified copy or extract under subsection (1).
A fee specified under subsection (3) must not be such as to amount to taxation.

section.heading: Use and disclosure of information obtained from the Registry

content.p: Use
A person must not use information to contact or send material to another person if that information:
is about the other person; and
was obtained from the Registry.
Disclosure
(2) A person (the first person) must not disclose information that:
is about another person; and
was obtained from the Registry; and
the first person knows is likely to be used to contact or send material to the other person.
Exceptions
Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply if the use or disclosure of the information is relevant to:
the holding of:
Australian carbon credit units; or
Kyoto units; or
safeguard mechanism credit units;
recorded in the Registry; or
the exercise of the rights attaching to those units.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (3) bears an evidential burden in relation to that matter.
Note: For evidential burden, see section 4.
Ancillary contraventions
A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (1) or (2); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (1) or (2); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (1) or (2); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (1) or (2).
Civil penalty provisions
(6) Subsections (1), (2) and (5) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 7 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.
The regulations may make further provision in relation to the Registry.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision requiring the holder of a Registry account to notify a matter to the Regulator.
Subsection (2) does not limit subsection (1).
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may:
(a) make provision for identifying Registry accounts that are restricted Registry accounts for the purposes of this section; and
restrict or limit the operation of restricted Registry accounts.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (3A) may:
prohibit, restrict or limit the transfer of units from a restricted Registry account; or
prohibit, restrict or limit the transfer of units to a restricted Registry account.
Subsection (3B) does not limit subsection (3A).
Subsections (3A) and (3B) do not limit subsection (1).
Section 28C does not limit subsections (3A) and (3B) of this section.
Requirement
If the holder of a Registry account is subject to a requirement under regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) or (2), the holder must comply with that requirement.
Ancillary contraventions
A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (4); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (4); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (4); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (4).
Civil penalty provisions
(6) Subsections (4) and (5) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 7 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.

section.heading: Suspension of operation of the Registry

content.p: The Regulator may temporarily suspend the operation of the Registry if the Regulator is satisfied that:
the suspension is required so that maintenance can be carried out; or
it is prudent to suspend the operation of the Registry in order to:
ensure the integrity of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise abuse of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise criminal activity involving the Registry.
If the Regulator suspends the operation of the Registry, the Regulator must publish a notice on the Regulator’s website informing the public of the suspension.
If the Regulator suspends the operation of the Registry, the Regulator may defer taking action in relation to the Registry until the suspension ends.

section.heading: Regulator may defer giving effect to a transfer instruction

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Regulator receives an instruction to transfer one or more:
Australian carbon credit units; or
Kyoto units; or
safeguard mechanism credit units;
to or from a Registry account kept in the name of a person.
Regulator may defer giving effect to the instruction

The Regulator may defer giving effect to the instruction, for a period that ends not later than the end of the fifth business day after the day on which the instruction was received, if the Regulator is satisfied that it is prudent to do so in order to:
ensure the integrity of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise abuse of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise criminal activity involving the Registry.
Prior notice not required
The Regulator is not required to give any prior notice of a deferral under subsection (2).
Other provisions
This section has effect despite:
any other provision of this Act; or
(b) anything in the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011.

section.heading: Regulator may refuse to give effect to a transfer instruction

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Regulator receives an instruction to transfer one or more:
Australian carbon credit units; or
Kyoto units; or
safeguard mechanism credit units;
to or from a Registry account kept in the name of a person.
Regulator may refuse to give effect to instruction
The Regulator may refuse to give effect to the instruction if the Regulator is satisfied that it is prudent to do so in order to:
ensure the integrity of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise abuse of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise criminal activity involving the Registry.
Notification
As soon as practicable after the Regulator refuses, under subsection (2), to give effect to the instruction, the Regulator must give written notice of the refusal to:
in any case—the person; or
if the instruction was given by another person—that other person.
A notice given to a person under subsection (3) must invite the person to request the Regulator to cease to refuse to give effect to the instruction.
A request under subsection (4) must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Regulator; and
set out the reason for the request.

If the person makes a request under subsection (4), the Regulator may, by written notice given to the person, require the person to give the Regulator, within the period specified in the notice, further information in connection with the request.
Prior notice not required
The Regulator is not required to give any prior notice of a refusal under subsection (2).
Decision on request
If the Regulator receives a request under subsection (4), the Regulator must:
cease to refuse to give effect to the instruction; or
decide to continue to refuse to give effect to the instruction.
The Regulator must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made under subsection (8):
if the Regulator requires the person to give further information under subsection (6) in relation to the request—within 7 days after the person gave the Regulator the information; or
otherwise—within 7 days after the request was made.
As soon as practicable after the Regulator makes a decision under subsection (8), the Regulator must notify the person, in writing, of the decision.
Other provisions
This section has effect despite:
any other provision of this Act; or
(b) anything in the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011.
Note: For additional powers of refusal, see:
paragraph 34(3)(a) of this Act; and
paragraph 35(3)(a) of this Act; and
subsection 36(2) of this Act.

section.heading: Conditions restricting or limiting the operation of Registry accounts

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a Registry account kept in the name of a person.
Imposition of conditions
The Regulator may, by written instrument, impose conditions restricting or limiting the operation of the Registry account for a specified period.
The Regulator may exercise the power conferred by subsection (2):
on the Regulator’s own initiative; or
on written request made to the Regulator by the person.
The Regulator must not make an instrument under subsection (2) unless the Regulator is satisfied that it is prudent to do so in order to:
ensure the integrity of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise abuse of the Registry; or
prevent, mitigate or minimise criminal activity involving the Registry.
A condition under subsection (2) may:
prohibit, restrict or limit the transfer of units from the Registry account; or
prohibit, restrict or limit the transfer of units to the Registry account.
Subsection (5) does not limit subsection (2).
Notification
As soon as practicable after making an instrument under subsection (2), the Regulator must give the person a copy of the instrument.
If an instrument under subsection (2) is made on the Regulator’s own initiative, the copy of the instrument must be accompanied by a notice inviting the person to request the Regulator to:
revoke the instrument; or
vary the instrument in the manner specified in the request.
Request
A request under paragraph (3)(b) or subsection (8) must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Regulator; and
set out the reason for the request.
Further information

If the person makes a request under subsection (8), the Regulator may, by written notice given to the person, require the person to give the Regulator, within the period specified in the notice, further information in connection with the request.
Prior notice not required
The Regulator is not required to give any prior notice of a decision to make an instrument under subsection (2).
Decision in relation to instrument made on own initiative
If the Regulator receives a request under subsection (8), the Regulator must:
if the request is to revoke the instrument:
revoke the instrument; or
decide not to revoke the instrument; or
if the request is to vary the instrument:
vary the instrument as requested; or
decide not to vary the instrument.
The Regulator must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made under subsection (12):
if the Regulator requires the person to give further information under subsection (10) in relation to the request—within 7 days after the person gave the Regulator the information; or
otherwise—within 7 days after the request was made.
As soon as practicable after the Regulator makes a decision under subsection (12), the Regulator must notify the person, in writing, of the decision.
Revocation of instrument made in response to a request
If:
an instrument is in force under subsection (2); and
the instrument was made in response to a request under paragraph (3)(b);
the Regulator must, at the written request of the person, revoke the instrument.

section.heading: Issue of Australia’s assigned amount units

content.p: Object
The object of this section is to provide for the issue of Australia’s assigned amount units for a commitment period.
Issue

The Secretary may, by written notice given to the Regulator, direct the Regulator to issue to the Commonwealth, in accordance with the Kyoto rules, a specified number of assigned amount units for a specified commitment period.
The Regulator must comply with a direction under subsection (2).
The Regulator is to issue an assigned amount unit by making an entry for the unit in a Commonwealth holding account.

This section does not, by implication, affect the validity of the issue of assigned amount units, where the units were issued before the commencement of this section under the executive power of the Commonwealth.
Object
The object of this section is to provide for the issue of Australia’s removal units.
Issue
The Secretary may, by written notice given to the Regulator, direct the Regulator to issue to the Commonwealth, in accordance with the Kyoto rules, a specified number of removal units.
The Regulator must comply with a direction under subsection (2).
The Regulator is to issue a removal unit by making an entry for the unit in a Commonwealth holding account.

This section does not, by implication, affect the validity of the issue of removal units, where the units were issued before the commencement of this section under the executive power of the Commonwealth.
The regulations may provide that the registered holder of a Kyoto unit:
is the legal owner of the unit; and
may, subject to this Act, deal with the unit as its legal owner and give good discharges for any consideration for any such dealing.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) only protect a person who deals with the registered holder of the unit as a purchaser:
in good faith for value; and
without notice of any defect in the title of the registered holder.
(1) For the purposes of this Act, if there is an entry for a Kyoto unit in a Registry account (the first Registry account) kept by a person (the first person):
(a) a transfer of the unit from the first Registry account to a Registry account kept by another person consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the first Registry account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the Registry account kept by the other person; and
(b) the transfer of the unit from the first Registry account to another Registry account kept by the first person consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the first Registry account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the other Registry account kept by the first person; and
(c) the transfer of the unit from the first Registry account to a foreign account kept by another person consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the first Registry account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the foreign account kept by the other person; and
(d) the transfer of the unit from the first Registry account to a foreign account kept by the first person consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the first Registry account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the foreign account kept by the first person.
(2) For the purposes of this Act, if there is an entry for a Kyoto unit in a foreign account, a transfer of the unit from the foreign account to a Registry account consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the foreign account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the Registry account.

(1) If a person (the first person) is the registered holder of one or more Kyoto units, the person may, by electronic notice transmitted to the Regulator, instruct the Regulator to transfer the units from the relevant Registry account kept by the person (the first Registry account) to:
a Registry account kept by another person; or
another Registry account kept by the first person.
An instruction under subsection (1) must set out:
the account number of the first Registry account; and
the account number of the Registry account mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b); and
such other information as is specified in the regulations.
Compliance with instruction
If the Regulator receives an instruction under subsection (1):
if the Regulator is satisfied that giving effect to the instruction would breach:
regulations made for the purposes of section 39 (Kyoto rules); or
regulations made for the purposes of section 41 (commitment period reserve); or
regulations made for the purposes of section 44 (Commonwealth Registry accounts);
the Regulator must, by written notice given to the first person, refuse to give effect to the instruction; and
if paragraph (a) does not apply—the Regulator must give effect to the instruction as soon as practicable after receiving it.
If the Regulator gives effect to an instruction under subsection (1), the Registry must set out a record of the instruction.
If the first person is the Commonwealth, the Minister may give an instruction under subsection (1) on behalf of the first person.

section.heading: Outgoing international transfers of Kyoto units

content.p: If:
there is in force a declaration under section 37 that Australia is in compliance with the emissions trading eligibility requirements under the Kyoto rules; and
(b) a person (the first person) is the registered holder of one or more Kyoto units;
the person may, by electronic notice transmitted to the Regulator, instruct the Regulator to transfer the units from the relevant Registry account kept by the person (the first Registry account) to:
a foreign account kept by another person; or
a foreign account kept by the first person.
An instruction under subsection (1) must set out:
the account number of the relevant Registry account kept by the first person; and
such other information as is specified in the regulations.
Compliance with instruction
If the Regulator receives an instruction under subsection (1):
if the Regulator is satisfied that giving effect to the instruction would breach:
regulations made for the purposes of section 39 (Kyoto rules); or
regulations made for the purposes of section 41 (commitment period reserve);
the Regulator must, by written notice given to the first person, refuse to give effect to the instruction; and
if paragraph (a) does not apply—the Regulator must take such steps as are required by regulations made for the purposes of section 39.
Regulations made for the purposes of section 39 may require the Regulator to remove the entry for the unit or units from the relevant Registry account.
Subsection (4) does not limit section 39.
If the Regulator takes steps under paragraph (3)(b) in relation to an instruction, the Registry must set out a record of the instruction.
If the first person is the Commonwealth, the Minister may give an instruction under subsection (1) on behalf of the first person.

section.heading: Incoming international transfers of Kyoto units

content.p: If:
there is in force a declaration under section 37 that Australia is in compliance with the emissions trading eligibility requirements under the Kyoto rules; and
the Regulator receives an instruction, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Kyoto rules, for the transfer of a Kyoto unit from a foreign account; and
the Kyoto unit is not specified in the regulations as a unit that cannot be transferred to a Registry account; and
making an entry for the Kyoto unit in the relevant Registry account would not breach regulations made for the purposes of section 39 (Kyoto rules); and
making an entry for the Kyoto unit in the relevant Registry account would not breach regulations made for the purposes of section 44 (Commonwealth Registry accounts);
the Regulator must make an entry for the Kyoto unit in the relevant Registry account.
Note: For specification by class, see subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003.
However, the Regulator may refuse to make an entry for the Kyoto unit in the relevant Registry account if the Regulator has reasonable grounds to suspect that the instruction is fraudulent.

section.heading: Compliance by Australia with emissions trading eligibility requirements under the Kyoto rules

content.p: Declaration

If the Minister is satisfied that Australia is in compliance with the eligibility requirements mentioned in paragraph 2 of the Annex to Decision 11/CMP.1 of the Meeting of the Kyoto Parties, the Minister must, by writing, declare that Australia is in compliance with the emissions trading eligibility requirements under the Kyoto rules.
Revocation of declaration
If:
a declaration is in force under subsection (1); and
the Minister is not satisfied that Australia is in compliance with the eligibility requirements mentioned in paragraph 2 of the Annex to Decision 11/CMP.1 of the Meeting of the Kyoto Parties;
the Minister must, by writing, revoke the declaration.
Declaration or revocation is not a legislative instrument
An instrument made under subsection (1) or (2) is not a legislative instrument.
The regulations may make provision for, or in relation to, giving effect to the Kyoto rules, so far as the Kyoto rules relate to:
the transfer of a Kyoto unit from a Registry account to a foreign account; or
the transfer of a Kyoto unit from a foreign account to a Registry account; or
the transfer of a Kyoto unit from a Registry account to a Commonwealth Registry account; or
the issue of a Kyoto unit; or
the conversion of an assigned amount unit, or a removal unit, to an emission reduction unit.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may:
prevent, restrict or limit the transfer of Kyoto units from a Registry account to:
a foreign account; or
a voluntary cancellation account; or
prevent, restrict or limit the transfer of Kyoto units from a foreign account to a Registry account.
Subsection (2) does not limit subsection (1).
Kyoto units for which carry-over is permitted
The regulations may make provision for, or in relation to, the following matters:
the identification of:
assigned amount units in Registry accounts; or
certified emission reductions (other than temporary certified emission reductions or long-term certified emission reductions) in Registry accounts; or
emission reduction units (other than emission reduction units that have been converted from removal units) in Registry accounts;
as Kyoto units for which carry-over is permitted subject to such limits or restrictions (if any) as are specified in the regulations;
the procedures for the carry-over of such Kyoto units;
requiring the Regulator to transfer from the relevant Registry account to a mandatory cancellation account any such Kyoto units that have not been carried over in accordance with those procedures.
Kyoto units for which carry-over is not permitted
The regulations may make provision for, or in relation to, the following matters:
the identification of Kyoto units for which carry-over is not permitted;

requiring the Regulator to transfer from the relevant Registry account to a mandatory cancellation account any such Kyoto units held in the Registry account at a time ascertained in accordance with the regulations.
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) must identify the following units issued in relation to the relevant commitment period as units for which carry-over is not permitted:
removal units;
temporary certified emission reductions;
long-term certified emission reductions;
emission reduction units that have been converted from removal units.
Kyoto rules
Regulations made for the purposes of this section must not be inconsistent with the Kyoto rules.
The regulations may make provision for, or in relation to, the management of Australia’s commitment period reserve.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may prevent, restrict or limit the transfer of Kyoto units from a Registry account to:
a foreign account; or
a voluntary cancellation account.

(3) Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) may prevent, restrict or limit the giving of instructions, under paragraph 154(1)(b) of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011, for the transfer of Kyoto Australian carbon credit units.

section.heading: Cancellation of temporary certified emission reductions or long-term certified emission reductions

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a person is the holder of a Registry account in which there is an entry for a temporary certified emission reduction or a long-term certified emission reduction; and
the temporary certified emission reduction or long-term certified emission reduction expires.
Transfer to mandatory cancellation account
The Regulator must, in accordance with the regulations, transfer the temporary certified emission reduction or long-term certified emission reduction to a mandatory cancellation account.

section.heading: Replacement of long-term certified emission reductions

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a person is the holder of a Registry account in which there is an entry for a long-term certified emission reduction; and
under the regulations, the person is required to replace the long-term certified emission reduction by a particular time ascertained in accordance with the regulations; and
the person breaches that requirement.
Transfer to mandatory cancellation account
The Regulator must, in accordance with the regulations, transfer the long-term certified emission reduction to a mandatory cancellation account.
Replacement of long-term certified emission reduction

(3) For the purposes of this section, if a long-term certified emission reduction relates to a clean development mechanism project, the replacement by the person of the long-term certified emission reduction consists of instructing the Regulator under section 34 to transfer:
an assigned amount unit; or
a removal unit; or
an emission reduction unit; or
a certified emission reduction (other than a temporary certified emission reduction or a long-term certified emission reduction); or
a long-term certified emission reduction relating to the project;
from a Registry account kept by the person to whichever of the following accounts is taken, under the regulations, to be the appropriate account:
the long-term certified emission reduction replacement (storage reversal) account;
the long-term certified emission reduction replacement (non-certification) account.
Identification of long-term certified emission reductions for which replacement is required
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(b) may make provision for, or in relation to, the identification of long-term certified emission reductions for which replacement is required.

section.heading: Restrictions on transfer of Kyoto units to a Commonwealth Registry account

content.p: The regulations may prevent, restrict or limit the transfer of Kyoto units from:
a Registry account; or
a foreign account;
to a Commonwealth Registry account.

section.heading: A registered Kyoto unit is personal property for certain purposes

content.p: Scope
This section applies if there is an entry for a Kyoto unit in a Registry account.
Personal property
For each of the following purposes:
(a) the purposes of the Bankruptcy Act 1966;
(b) the purposes of Chapter 5 of the Corporations Act 2001;
the purposes of the law relating to wills, intestacy and deceased estates;
a prescribed purpose;
the unit is personal property and, subject to section 47, is transmissible by will and by devolution by operation of law.

section.heading: Registration of equitable interests in relation to Kyoto units

content.p: The regulations may make provision for or in relation to the registration in the Registry of equitable interests in relation to Kyoto units.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply to an equitable interest that is a security interest within the meaning of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009, and to which that Act applies.

section.heading: Equitable interests in relation to a Kyoto unit

content.p: This Act does not affect:
the creation of; or
any dealings with; or
the enforcement of;
equitable interests in relation to a Kyoto unit.
Subsection (1) is enacted for the avoidance of doubt.

section.heading: Transmission of registered Kyoto units by operation of law etc.

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
under section 45, a Kyoto unit is personal property for a particular purpose; and
(b) the unit is transmitted from a person (the transferor) to another person (the transferee) by any lawful means for that purpose.
Effect of transmission
The transmission is of no force until the Regulator transfers the unit under subsection (7) or (8).
Declaration of transmission
The transferee must, within 90 days after the transmission, give the Regulator:
a declaration of transmission; and
such evidence of transmission as is specified in the regulations.
A declaration of transmission must be made in accordance with the regulations.

If the transferee does not already have a Registry account, the declaration of transmission must be accompanied by a request under regulations made for the purposes of subsection 10(1) for the Regulator to open a Registry account in the name of the transferee.
If the Regulator is satisfied that special circumstances warrant the extension of the 90-day period mentioned in subsection (2), the Regulator may extend that period.
The Regulator may exercise the power conferred by subsection (5):
on written application being made to the Regulator by the transferee; or
on the Regulator’s own initiative.
Transfer of unit—transferee already has a Registry account

If the transferee already has a Registry account, the Regulator must, as soon as practicable after receiving the declaration of transmission, transfer the unit from the relevant Registry account kept by the transferor to a Registry account kept by the transferee.
Transfer of unit—transferee does not have a Registry account
If:
the transferee does not already have a Registry account; and
in accordance with the request under regulations made for the purposes of subsection 10(1), the Regulator has opened a Registry account in the name of the transferee;

the Regulator must, as soon as practicable after opening the Registry account, transfer the unit from the relevant Registry account kept by the transferor to the Registry account kept by the transferee.
Record
If the Regulator transfers the unit under subsection (7) or (8), the Registry must set out a record of the declaration of transmission.
When the transferee is the Commonwealth
If the transferee is the Commonwealth, the Minister may give:
the declaration of transmission; and
the evidence mentioned in paragraph (2)(b);
on behalf of the transferee.
Notification
If:
the Regulator decides to:
extend the 90-day period mentioned in subsection (2); or
refuse to extend the 90-day period mentioned in subsection (2); and
the Regulator made the decision in response to an application;
the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant.
• This Part sets out rules about the ownership, transfer and transmission of safeguard mechanism credit units.

section.heading: A safeguard mechanism credit unit is personal property

content.p: A safeguard mechanism credit unit is personal property and, subject to sections 48D and 48E, is transmissible by assignment, by will and by devolution by operation of law.

section.heading: Ownership of safeguard mechanism credit units

content.p: The registered holder of a safeguard mechanism credit unit:
is the legal owner of the unit; and
(b) may, subject to this Act and the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act 2007, deal with the unit as its legal owner and give good discharges for any consideration for any such dealing.
Subsection (1) only protects a person who deals with the registered holder of the unit as a purchaser:
in good faith for value; and
without notice of any defect in the title of the registered holder.

section.heading: Transfer of safeguard mechanism credit units

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, if there is an entry for a safeguard mechanism credit unit in a Registry account (the first Registry account) kept by a person (the first person):
(a) a transfer of the unit from the first Registry account to a Registry account kept by another person consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the first Registry account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the Registry account kept by the other person; and
(b) a transfer of the unit from the first Registry account to another Registry account kept by the first person consists of:
the removal of the entry for the unit from the first Registry account; and
the making of an entry for the unit in the other Registry account kept by the first person.

section.heading: Transmission of safeguard mechanism credit units by assignment

content.p: A transmission by assignment of a safeguard mechanism credit unit for which there is an entry in a Registry account is of no force until:

the transferor, by electronic notice transmitted to the Regulator, instructs the Regulator to transfer the unit from the relevant Registry account kept by the transferor to a Registry account kept by the transferee; and
the Regulator complies with that instruction.
An instruction under paragraph (1)(a) must set out:
the account number of the transferor’s Registry account; and
the account number of the transferee’s Registry account.
If the Regulator receives an instruction under paragraph (1)(a), the Regulator must comply with the instruction as soon as practicable after receiving it.
The Registry must set out a record of each instruction under paragraph (1)(a).
If the transferor is the Commonwealth, the Minister may give an instruction under paragraph (1)(a) on behalf of the transferor.

section.heading: Transmission of safeguard mechanism credit units by operation of law etc.

content.p: Scope

(1) This section applies if a safeguard mechanism credit unit for which there is an entry in a Registry account is transmitted from a person (the transferor) to another person (the transferee) by any lawful means other than by a transfer under section 48D.
Effect of transmission
The transmission is of no force until the Regulator transfers the safeguard mechanism credit unit under subsection (8) or (9).
Declaration of transmission
The transferee must, within 90 days after the transmission, give the Regulator:
a declaration of transmission; and
such evidence of transmission as is specified in the legislative rules.
A declaration of transmission must be made in accordance with the legislative rules.

If the transferee does not already have a Registry account, the declaration of transmission must be accompanied by a request, under regulations made for the purposes of subsection 10(1), for the Regulator to open a Registry account in the name of the transferee.
If the Regulator is satisfied that special circumstances warrant the extension of the 90-day period mentioned in subsection (3), the Regulator may extend that period.
The Regulator may exercise the power conferred by subsection (6):
on written application being made to the Regulator by the transferee; or
on the Regulator’s own initiative.

The following is a simplified outline of this Part:
• Pecuniary penalties are payable for contraventions of civil penalty provisions.
In this Part:
Court means:
the Federal Court; or
a court of a State or Territory that has jurisdiction in relation to matters arising under this Act.
If a Court is satisfied that a person has contravened a civil penalty provision, the Court may order the person to pay the Commonwealth a pecuniary penalty.
(2) An order under subsection (1) is to be known as a civil penalty order.
Determining amount of pecuniary penalty
In determining the pecuniary penalty, the Court may have regard to all relevant matters, including:
the nature and extent of the contravention; and
the nature and extent of any loss or damage suffered as a result of the contravention; and
the circumstances in which the contravention took place; and
whether the person has previously been found by a court in proceedings under this Act to have engaged in any similar conduct; and
the extent to which the person has co-operated with the authorities; and
if the person is a body corporate:
the level of the employees, officers or agents of the body corporate involved in the contravention; and
whether the body corporate exercised due diligence to avoid the contravention; and
whether the body corporate had a corporate culture conducive to compliance.
The pecuniary penalty payable under subsection (1) by a body corporate must not exceed:
in the case of a contravention of subsection 26(1), (2) or (5)—500 penalty units for each contravention; or
otherwise—10,000 penalty units for each contravention.
The pecuniary penalty payable under subsection (1) by a person other than a body corporate must not exceed:
in the case of a contravention of subsection 26(1), (2) or (5)—100 penalty units for each contravention; or
otherwise—2,000 penalty units for each contravention.
Civil enforcement of penalty

A pecuniary penalty is a civil debt payable to the Commonwealth. The Commonwealth may enforce the civil penalty order as if it were an order made in civil proceedings against the person to recover a debt due by the person. The debt arising from the order is taken to be a judgement debt.

section.heading: Who may apply for a civil penalty order

section.heading: Civil evidence and procedure rules for civil penalty orders

content.p: The Court must apply the rules of evidence and procedure for civil matters when hearing proceedings for a civil penalty order.

The Court must not make a civil penalty order against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision if the person has been convicted of an offence constituted by conduct that is substantially the same as the conduct constituting the contravention.
Proceedings for a civil penalty order against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision are stayed if:
criminal proceedings are started or have already been started against the person for an offence; and
(b) the offence is constituted by conduct that is substantially the same as the conduct alleged to constitute the contravention.
The proceedings for the order may be resumed if the person is not convicted of the offence. Otherwise, the proceedings for the order are dismissed.

Criminal proceedings may be started against a person for conduct that is substantially the same as conduct constituting a contravention of a civil penalty provision regardless of whether a civil penalty order has been made against the person.

section.heading: Evidence given in proceedings for a civil penalty order not admissible in criminal proceedings

content.p: Evidence of information given, or evidence of production of documents, by an individual is not admissible in criminal proceedings against the individual if:

the individual previously gave the evidence or produced the documents in proceedings for a civil penalty order against the individual for a contravention of a civil penalty provision (whether or not the order was made); and
the conduct alleged to constitute the offence is substantially the same as the conduct that was claimed to constitute the contravention.
However, this does not apply to a criminal proceeding in respect of the falsity of the evidence given by the individual in the proceedings for the civil penalty order.
A person is not liable to have a civil penalty order made against the person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision if:
at or before the time of the conduct constituting the contravention, the person:
considered whether or not facts existed; and
was under a mistaken but reasonable belief about those facts; and
had those facts existed, the conduct would not have constituted a contravention of the civil penalty provision.
For the purposes of subsection (1), a person may be regarded as having considered whether or not facts existed if:
the person had considered, on a previous occasion, whether those facts existed in the circumstances surrounding that occasion; and
the person honestly and reasonably believed that the circumstances surrounding the present occasion were the same, or substantially the same, as those surrounding the previous occasion.
A person who wishes to rely on subsection (1) or (2) in proceedings for a civil penalty order bears an evidential burden in relation to that matter.
Scope
This section applies to proceedings for a civil penalty order against a person for a contravention of any of the following civil penalty provisions:
subsection 26(1);
subsection 26(2);
subsection 27(4).
State of mind
In the proceedings, it is not necessary to prove:
the person’s intention; or
the person’s knowledge; or
the person’s recklessness; or
the person’s negligence; or
any other state of mind of the person.
Subsection (2) does not affect the operation of section 78.

If an act or thing is required, under a civil penalty provision of this Act, to be done within a particular period, or before a particular time, then the obligation to do that act or thing continues (even if the period has expired or the time has passed) until the act or thing is done.

A person who contravenes subsection 27(4), so far as that subsection relates to a requirement mentioned in subsection 27(2), commits a separate contravention of that provision in respect of each day (including a day of the making of a relevant civil penalty order or any subsequent day) during which the contravention continues.

The pecuniary penalty payable under subsection 69(1) for such a separate contravention in respect of a particular day must not exceed 5% of the maximum pecuniary penalty that could have been imposed for the contravention if subsection (2) of this section had not been enacted.

section.heading: Applications for reconsideration of decisions made by delegates of the Regulator

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a reviewable decision if the decision is made by a delegate of the Regulator.
Application
A person affected by a reviewable decision who is dissatisfied with the decision may apply to the Regulator for the Regulator to reconsider the decision.
The application must:
be in a form approved in writing by the Regulator; and
set out the reasons for the application; and
be accompanied by the fee (if any) specified in the regulations.
The application must be made within:
28 days after the applicant is informed of the decision; or
if, either before or after the end of that period of 28 days, the Regulator extends the period within which the application may be made—the extended period.
An approved form of an application may provide for verification by statutory declaration of statements in applications.
A fee specified under paragraph (3)(c) must not be such as to amount to taxation.
Upon receiving such an application, the Regulator must:
reconsider the decision; and
affirm, vary or revoke the decision.
The Regulator’s decision on reconsideration of a decision has effect as if it had been made under the provision under which the original decision was made.
The Regulator must give to the applicant a written notice stating the Regulator’s decision on the reconsideration.
Within 28 days after making the decision on the reconsideration, the Regulator must give the applicant a written statement of the Regulator’s reasons for the decision.
The Regulator must make its decision on reconsideration of a decision within 90 days after receiving an application for reconsideration.

The Regulator is taken, for the purposes of this Part, to have made a decision affirming the original decision if the Regulator has not informed the applicant of its decision on the reconsideration before the end of the period of 90 days.

content.p: Applications may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal to review a reviewable decision if the Regulator has affirmed or varied the decision under section 84.
